Source: https://github.com/helixnow/deep-student
Commit: 635216503c0b34bdf812e17942e0f09f51872e6f

Seven original files from src/essay-grading are archived byte-for-byte in
upstream/. source-manifest.json records SHA-256 and fixed-commit Git blob IDs.
build.cjs transpiles the unchanged files using TypeScript 5.9.3 to CommonJS
ES2022 JavaScript. No Tauri, VFS, provider, UI, npm runtime dependency or
upstream application entry point is included.

The upstream root license is GNU AGPLv3; the upstream third-party licensing
document states AGPL-3.0-or-later. The original root license and original
third-party notices are retained unchanged. Their full inventory describes
the upstream application, not this candidate's actual dependency closure.
The candidate has only local JavaScript modules and Node 24.14.0 builtins.

New project-owned wrapper: raw UTF-8 draft SHA-256/revision/role binding,
Unicode scalar length and codepoint bounds, strict rubric/raw score and
terminal-event validation, exact and unique annotation context guards,
single XML transport decoding, reference-only typed results and a bounded
single-request JSON stdin+EOF/stdout helper. It retains upstream parser
results as diagnostic candidates while refusing silent score adjustment or
ambiguous anchors as reliable evaluation. It never overwrites a draft.

Only validate_feedback is exposed by helper.cjs. The pure revision proposal,
round-switch/fingerprint and immutable assessment fixture functions are
investigation fixtures, not an authoritative business store or public RPC.
Formal Artifact revision, operation identity, persistence, CAS, cancellation,
late callback admission, user self-assessment/override and model execution
remain the owning project's responsibility.

Original trim/truncation, image reads, dynamic latest-round lookup, database
transactions, retry/provider pipeline and treating an incomplete response as
complete merely because it contains a score end tag are not migrated.

This notice records provenance and changes. It does not establish that this
candidate passed product, real-model or user-experience acceptance.
